senses.gloss: f.(b. h. רְפֻאוֹת; רָפָא)healing, cure; medicine, remedy.
units: <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 17b:9">R. Hash. 17ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 6:10">Is. VI, 10</cite>) <he>איזהו דבר שצריך ר׳ וכ׳</he> what is that which needs to be remedied? It is a divine decree (which may be averted by man’s repentance).

<cite ref="Megillah 13b:12">Meg. 13ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Esther 3:1">Esth. III, 1</cite>) <he>אחר … ר׳ למכה</he> after the Lord had prepared the remedy for the wound (the means of delivery from the affliction).
<cite ref="Esther 3:1">Ib.</cite> <he>אין הקב״ה … ר׳ תחילה</he> the Lord does not strike Israel, unless he has prepared the remedy in advance.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 6:10">Sabb. VI, 10</cite> <he>משום ר׳</he> as a medicinal amulet.
<cite ref="Shabbat 67a:14">Ib. 67ᵃ</cite> <he>כל דבר שיש בו משום ר׳</he> whatever is done for medicinal purposes.

<cite ref="Shabbat 67a:15">Ib.</cite> <he>מאי ר׳ קעביד</he> what remedy can he effect by it? <cite ref="Berakhot 60a:11-28">Ber. 60ᵃ</cite> (a prayer before blood-letting) <he>יהי רצון … לר׳ ותרפאני … ורְפוּאָתְךָ אמת</he> may it be thy will, O Lord my God, that this procedure be a cure to me, and heal thou me, for thou art a faithfully healing God, and thy healing is real; a. fr.—<he>רְפוּאַת ממון</he>, <he>רפואת נפש</he>, v. <cite ref="T00678"><he>רִיפּוּי</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: R’fuah, prayer for health, name of the eighth section of the Prayer of Benedictions (תפלה).
units: <cite ref="Megillah 17b:11">Meg. 17ᵇ</cite> <he>לימא ר׳ בתרה דתשובה</he> why not recite R’fuah immediately after T’shubah (prayer for forgiveness)? <cite ref="Megillah 17b:10-14">Ib.</cite> <he>ומה … ר׳ בשמינית</he> what reason had they to make R’fuah the eighth benediction? <cite ref="Megillah 17b:12">Ib.</cite> (ref. to Is. l. c.) <he>ההוא לאו ר׳ … אלא ר׳ דסליחה</he> this is not healing referring to diseases, but a healing (from sin) through forgiveness; a. e.—Pl. <cite ref="T00937"><he>רְפוּאוֹת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Pesachim 4:9">Pes. IV, 9</cite> (<cite ref="Pesachim 56a:2">56ᵃ</cite>) <he>גנז ספר ר׳</he> he suppressed a book of remedies (charms and incantations).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 1:3:5">Y. R. Hash. I, 57ᵇ</cite> <he>נרתיק של ר׳</he> a medicine chest.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 5:2:3">Y. Ber. V, 9ᵇ</cite> top; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 1:1:5">Y. Taan. I, 63ᵈ</cite> top; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Yoma 86a:14">Yoma 86ᵃ</cite> <he>גדולה … ר׳ לעולם</he> (some ed. <cite ref="T00928"><he>רִפְאוּת</he></cite>; Ms. O. <cite ref="T00933"><he>רְפוּאָה</he></cite>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 80) repentance is a great thing, for it brings healing (delivery) to the world; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 269:1">Yalk. Jer. 269</cite> <cite ref="T00933"><he>רפואה</he></cite>.
